meta.title: Reading and influences
meta.note: The order of these links changes from time to time. That is intentional. Learning is rarely linear, and neither is change.

tiers.label: Start here
tiers.microCopy: A way in, not a conclusion.

items.name: Harvard Business Review
items.annotation: Widely shared thinking on leadership and management, useful as a common reference point even when it oversimplifies.

items.name: London Business School Think
items.annotation: Research-led writing that treats leadership as a systemic and collective practice rather than a personal trait.

items.name: Nesta
items.annotation: UK-focused innovation work that connects systems change, public value, and emerging technology.

items.name: Government Digital Service
items.annotation: Practical guidance rooted in real delivery, showing what change looks like inside constrained public systems.

tiers.label: Go deeper
tiers.microCopy: When the simple explanations stop working.

items.name: MIT Sloan Management Review
items.annotation: Serious analysis of digital transformation, organisational learning, and why technology rarely delivers on its own.

items.name: Oxford Review
items.annotation: Evidence-based management writing that challenges intuition, hype, and fashionable shortcuts.

items.name: Academy of Management Perspectives
items.annotation: Translational theory explaining why rational change efforts so often fail in real organisations.

items.name: Institute for Government
items.annotation: Clear-eyed analysis of how government actually works, including incentives, constraints, and trade-offs.

tiers.label: Challenge your assumptions
tiers.microCopy: This may change how you see the problem.

items.name: Evidence-Based Change (Fielding Graduate University)
items.annotation: Work in the Argyris and Schön tradition, focused on inquiry, defensive routines, and double-loop learning.

items.name: Santa Fe Institute
items.annotation: Complexity science applied to organisations and systems, challenging linear planning assumptions.

items.name: AI Now Institute
items.annotation: Critical research on AI, power, governance, and social impact that resists techno-neutral narratives.

items.name: Society for Organizational Learning
items.annotation: Systems thinking in practice, including its tensions, failures, and political realities.
